page: Microsoft Azure E20as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz, configured with 10 physical cores and 2 threads per core to deliver 20 dedicated vCPUs. It features a cache architecture with 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, supporting cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets.

Memory capacity is configured at 160.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB allocated per virtual core. The server includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data, and features no hardware graphics accelerators. Benchmark testing demonstrates strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng and top-quartile PassMark memory results. Synthetic memory throughput tests show 77.0 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 44.38 GB/sec for large-block writes.

In execution workloads, the E20as_v5 maintains middle-tier throughput across multi-core tests, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,461 and processing 20.32 million Redis SET operations per second. Light inference using small 135M parameter models demonstrates strong text generation rates, whereas larger 70B parameter models show constrained prompt processing due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. Cost efficiency reflects high memory density per compute core, balanced against the operational requirement to provision remote storage.

The instance is suited for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caching systems, data analytics pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise software deployments that require significant RAM allocations without massive parallel CPU footprints.
description: Microsoft Azure E20as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. It provides 20 dedicated vCPUs across 10 physical cores and 160.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring network-attached storage for persistent storage operations. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier PassMark memory scores and strong single-core stress-ng performance, accompanied by consistent middle-tier multi-core compute metrics, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,461 and 20.32 million Redis SET operations per second. Small-model machine learning inference achieves robust generation speeds, but large-model processing remains hardware-limited. The E20as_v5 provides economical memory capacity relative to compute allocations, making it well-matched for in-memory databases, large caching layers, and enterprise memory-intensive applications.
